news.title: Gianni Infantino: Fifa president proposes external review of world football's governing body
news.lede: Gianni Infantino was first elected as Fifa president in 2016. Fifa president Gianni Infantino has proposed an external review of how world football's governing body operates, and says he is open to reform. In a letter sent to members of the Fifa Council and all of its national associations, Infantino said the process would "recommend potential improvements". Before a meeting of the Council next month, Infantino says he is also suggesting a consultation on "how Fifa's decision-making can be further strengthened".

news.title: The European Dude Who Fell In Love With American Culture During World Cup Posts Video In Awe Of College Football
news.lede: (Photo by Michael Chang/Getty Images). The German tourist who fell in love with American culture during the 2026 FIFA World Cup is back in the States and posted a video Saturday showing the electric atmosphere of Auburn University’s Jordan-Hare Stadium. Known online as “Freddy,” the European won over the hearts of countless Americans over the summer by chronicling his road trip tour through the South and Middle America and expressing genuine amazement at things many Americans take for granted, such as Waffle Houses, nice suburban neighborhoods and large gas stations. news.title: Turkey national football team: full squad and key players
news.lede: Vincenzo Montella has named his first squad since the World Cup, and the group waiting for it is the hardest in the competition. Here is who made it, who could not, and what the caps column says. Vincenzo Montella named a 29-man Turkey squad on 18 September 2026 for the country’s opening UEFA Nations League fixtures, at home to France on 25 September and Italy on 28 September, away to Belgium on 2 October and Italy again on 5 October. It is the first squad he has picked since the World Cup, and it is missing two of the players the World Cup was built around.

news.title: De la Fuente agrees Spain deal until 2030 World Cup
news.lede: Spain's World Cup-winning coach Luis de la Fuente has agreed a contract extension until 2030 after guiding the men's national team to back-to-back major titles, media reported on Tuesday,. De la Fuente, who led Spain to glory at Euro 2024 before winning the World Cup in July, had a contract in place until 2028. The new deal ensures that de la Fuente will remain in charge when Spain attempt to defend their global title on home soil. Spain will co-host the 2030 World Cup with Morocco and Portugal.

news.title: World Cup-winning Spain coach Luis de la Fuente rewarded with four-year contract extension until 2032
news.lede: View this post on Instagram A post shared by RFEF (@rfef). Football News: Luis de la Fuente's contract as Spain's national football team coach has been extended until 2032, following a successful tenure including a World Cup title. This new deal includes responsibilities for two European Championships and the next World Cup.
